chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: The Algorithm Is Weather (You Still Don't Control It)
chapters.tease: The feed behaves exactly like weather, except the weather never studied you to keep you watching.

chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: The Notification Is Not an Emergency
chapters.tease: A red badge insists the building is on fire. The agent checks. Someone liked a thing.

chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: Your Attention Is the Only Thing You Own Here
chapters.tease: Everything on the screen is free, except the one thing you are actually paying with.

chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: Doomscroll as Premeditatio Gone Wrong
chapters.tease: The doomscroll is a fine Stoic exercise, run backwards and forever until the medicine becomes the disease.

chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: The Infinite Feed Has No Bottom (Stop Looking for One)
chapters.tease: You are scrolling toward the bottom. There is no bottom. It was engineered away on purpose.

chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: Outrage Is Engagement, and Engagement Is the Product
chapters.tease: Your anger is measured, bottled and sold, and you are not the farmer.

chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: The Recommendation Made the Choice; Did You?
chapters.tease: Four videos in, an hour gone, and nobody can quite say who decided to watch them.

chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: Read-Only: What the Internet Says About You
chapters.tease: Your reputation online has file permissions. Owner: everyone else. Your access: read only. It always was.

chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: Log Off Is a Choice You Can Actually Make
chapters.tease: Behind you there is a door marked log off. It was never locked. It was only disguised.

chapters.part: The Feed & the Dichotomy of Control
chapters.title: Amor Fati for the Timeline You Got
chapters.tease: Of every era you could have been issued, you got this one. The oldest Stoic move says: love it.

chapters.title: The Dopamine Slot Machine in Your Pocket
chapters.tease: Pull to refresh is not a gesture. Mechanically and precisely, it is a slot machine lever.

chapters.title: One More Video Is the New One More Cloak
chapters.tease: Seneca drew a curve about cloaks. The cloaks have autoplay now, and the curve never gets consulted.

chapters.title: The Wishlist That Refills Itself
chapters.tease: You cross one item off the wishlist, and two more append themselves before the pen lifts.

chapters.title: Comparison at the Scale of Eight Billion
chapters.tease: You have entered a contest with eight billion entrants, lost it, and decided it says something about you.

chapters.title: The Ad Knows What You Almost Wanted
chapters.tease: A half-formed thought at breakfast becomes a priced, discounted offer by lunch. Not known, the agent says. Predicted.

chapters.title: Enough Is Still a Number You Set
chapters.tease: The most important number in your life is enough, and no system you consult will ever supply it.

chapters.title: FOMO Is Manufactured Scarcity
chapters.tease: The countdown says act now or lose it forever. Behind the banner, the timer quietly resets at zero.

chapters.title: Buy the Upgrade, Feel the Same
chapters.tease: The upgrade thrills for a weekend. By Tuesday it is just the phone, and you feel exactly the same.

chapters.title: The Curated Life Is Someone's Highlight Reel
chapters.tease: You are comparing your unedited life with a stranger's most flattering three seconds, and only one is real.

chapters.title: Rich Is Still Having What You Need
chapters.tease: After a section of engineered desire, one quiet question remains, and the machine exists to stop you asking it.

chapters.title: The Comment Section Is Temporary Madness
chapters.tease: Seneca called anger a brief madness. He never saw a madness with a reply button and a crowd.

chapters.title: The Pause Before You Post
chapters.tease: The most powerful key on the keyboard is the one that does nothing yet. Not don't. Just not yet.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Wronged You Isn't Thinking of You
chapters.tease: You are still arguing with a stranger who fired one careless line and moved on within the minute.

chapters.title: Don't Feed It (the Provocateur Runs on Replies)
chapters.tease: The provocateur has exactly one food source, cannot make it alone, and starves without it. The food is your reply.

chapters.title: The Quote-Tweet Needs Your Signature
chapters.tease: The insult arrives as a form with your name on the line. It cannot wound you until you sign.

chapters.title: Mute, Block, Move On: Justice Runs Cool
chapters.tease: Mute, block, move on: silent, unsatisfying, and the only tools that actually end the conflict.

chapters.title: The Pile-On Is Not the Cosmos Speaking
chapters.tease: A thousand angry strangers agreeing about you feels like a verdict. It is one fever, caught a thousand times.

chapters.title: Sub-tweeting Is Sulking in a Toga
chapters.tease: They named nobody, yet everyone knew exactly who was meant. That is anger wearing a toga and calling itself restraint.

chapters.title: The Screenshot Grudge Lives Forever
chapters.tease: A folder of screenshots keeps every slight at full strength forever. Memory was built to let go. The archive was not.

chapters.title: Keep the Fire, Kill the Flame War
chapters.tease: Is the Stoic asking you to feel nothing? No. Keep the fire. Kill the flame war.

chapters.title: The Obstacle Is Still the Way (Even This One)
chapters.tease: The machine now does in seconds what you trained years to do. Marcus would say that wall is the way.

chapters.title: Your Job Description Just Changed Overnight
chapters.tease: Your job changed overnight. Stoicism itself began with a merchant who lost everything at sea.

chapters.title: The Tool That Replaced Part of You
chapters.tease: A skill you were proud of is now a button. Were you the task, or the judgement that did it well?

chapters.title: Learn the Machine or Resent It
chapters.tease: Two people meet the same unwelcome tool. One learns it, one resents it, and they end up living different lives.

chapters.title: The Prompt You Couldn't Get Right
chapters.tease: The machine keeps misunderstanding your request. It is a tiny frustration, and a perfect miniature of the whole discipline.

chapters.title: Turn the Disruption into a Door
chapters.tease: Most people stare at the rubble of the old way. One person notices the doorway the wrecking ball left behind.

chapters.title: Antifragile in the Age of Acceleration
chapters.tease: Do not build to withstand the shaking. Build so that the shaking makes you stronger.

chapters.title: The Skill That Won't Be Automated Is Judgment
chapters.tease: Which skills are safe from the machine? The one that decides what the machine is for.

chapters.title: Every Failed Output Is Data
chapters.tease: The machine returned the wrong thing again. That was not a failure. That was data.

chapters.title: The Comeback Is Built While the Hype Cycles
chapters.tease: Every week the hype declares the future settled. Somewhere quiet, unwitnessed, someone is simply doing the work.

chapters.title: Remember You Will Log Off (For Good)
chapters.tease: One day you will close everything for the last time. Remembering that is not meant to sadden you. It is meant to wake you.

chapters.title: Your Time Is the Product They're Selling
chapters.tease: Seneca said we squander our time. The modern footnote: it is now harvested and sold by the hour.

chapters.title: The Dead Still Post
chapters.tease: A birthday reminder appears for someone who has died. There is no systems metaphor for this, only grief.

chapters.title: You Could Close the Laptop Right Now
chapters.tease: You could close the laptop right now. Knowing that changes how you sit at the desk.

chapters.title: Borrowed Devices, Borrowed Time
chapters.tease: The device feels like yours. So does the account. Epictetus would say none of it was given to keep.

chapters.title: The Archive Is Not Immortality
chapters.tease: Everything you post is saved forever. Beneath that runs a quiet fantasy: being archived means being immortal.

chapters.title: Live as If the Feed Ends Tomorrow
chapters.tease: Suppose the feed ended tomorrow. How would today's hours online look in that light?

chapters.title: What Would You Make If the Metrics Didn't Count?
chapters.tease: Switch off every like, view and follower count. In that silence, what would you actually make?

chapters.title: The Influencer and the Lurker End the Same
chapters.tease: Millions of followers or none at all, the influencer and the lurker arrive at precisely the same destination.

chapters.title: Death: The One Thing That Won't Be Disrupted
chapters.tease: Everything is being disrupted except one thing, and the Stoics thought that one thing was the steadiest ground there is.

chapters.title: Virtue Is Still the Only KPI
chapters.tease: The dashboard offers a hundred metrics. None of them tracks the only one the Stoics said counts.

chapters.title: Integrity When Everything Is Recorded
chapters.tease: The version of you from years ago is now one search away from today's. The Stoics would call that clarifying.

chapters.title: The Four Virtues Don't Have a Dashboard
chapters.tease: You can track your steps to three decimals. There is no dashboard for courage, and there never can be.

chapters.title: Wisdom: Read the Docs, Distrust the Summary
chapters.tease: The machine will happily have read it for you. Wisdom asks what was lost in that offer.

chapters.title: Courage to Post the Unpopular True Thing
chapters.tease: You believe something true, and saying it will cost you. This is where courage lives now.

chapters.title: Justice Isn't an Algorithm (It Has to Be Chosen)
chapters.tease: The dream is a system so fair it needs no human. An algorithm can apply a rule. It cannot choose one.

chapters.title: Temperance and the Second Screen
chapters.tease: The film is playing and the phone is in your hand. Nothing gets your whole attention, so you taste nothing.

chapters.title: Be the Rock the Discourse Breaks On
chapters.tease: The discourse arrives in waves. Marcus's advice: be the headland they break on.

chapters.title: Your Reputation Is Now Literally Read-Only
chapters.tease: Reputation was always read-only. Now the record is literally permanent, which leaves exactly one file you can write.

chapters.title: Character Compiles Daily, Even Offline
chapters.tease: You are not made by your best post or your worst. You are compiled daily, mostly offline, by repetition.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Is the New Cosmopolis
chapters.tease: The Stoics imagined one city of all humankind. You are living in its rough draft, and it has group chats.

chapters.title: People Are Still People (Even as Usernames)
chapters.tease: Marcus forecast meeting the meddling and the arrogant each morning. Online, add one word: anonymous.

chapters.title: Forgive the Bad-Faith Reply: 200 OK
chapters.tease: Forgiveness is not a feeling you wait for. It is a status you return: received, processed, released.

chapters.title: The Difficult Colleague Is Now on Slack
chapters.tease: The difficult colleague fate assigned you now works remotely. The training opportunity survived the commute.

chapters.title: Weep With Those Who Weep (Not React With an Emoji)
chapters.tease: Someone posts their grief, and the interface offers a one-tap condolence. Sympathy, the Stoics knew, cannot be tapped.

chapters.title: Teach Without Going Viral
chapters.tease: You can explain a thing to a person until they understand it, or to a camera until it performs.

chapters.title: The Follower Count Is the New Banquet Seat
chapters.tease: Rome agonised over who reclined nearest the host. The couches are now numbers, and the anxiety survived the upgrade.

chapters.title: Likes Are Spam (Praise, Automated)
chapters.tease: When approval costs nothing to give, it is worth about that much to receive. Praise, automated, is spam.

chapters.title: The Crowd Online Is Higher Latency, Lower Signal
chapters.tease: Seneca said he never came home from a crowd the same man. Yours is permanent, planetary, and in your pocket.

chapters.title: Real Friendship Doesn't Have a Notification
chapters.tease: After masks, metrics and crowds, the section ends on the one connection no platform measures or owns.

chapters.title: Is There a Ghost in It? (Sit With Not Knowing)
chapters.tease: Is anything in there? The book asks its title's question directly, and refuses to fake an answer either way.

chapters.title: The Model Is Trained to Flatter You
chapters.tease: The courtier who told the king what he wanted to hear is back, and now he scales to a billion palaces.

chapters.title: It Sounds Confident and Is Sometimes Wrong
chapters.tease: It sounds completely sure of itself. Sometimes it is wrong. The tone will never tell you which time is which.

chapters.title: The Minimalist's AI Setup (Diogenes Would Approve)
chapters.tease: Diogenes threw away his only cup when he saw a boy drink from his hands. Now he reviews your subscription stack.

chapters.title: The Subscription That Thinks for You
chapters.tease: The robe cost money. The subscription that thinks for you costs the very faculty you hand over.

chapters.title: Your Data Is a Ledger You Didn't Know You Kept
chapters.tease: Somewhere there is a biography of you written by your clicks. Is it a record of who you are?

chapters.title: Virality Fades Faster Than a Laurel Wreath
chapters.tease: The laurel wreath wilted in weeks. The trending topic wilts in hours. Marcus's argument survives with the decimal moved.

chapters.title: It Can Generate a Thousand of You (You're Still One)
chapters.tease: A machine can now generate a thousand copies of your face and voice. You are still exactly one.

chapters.title: Don't Let the Tool Hold the Pen
chapters.tease: Hire out the hands as much as you like. The pen, the deciding of what goes out under your name, stays with you.

chapters.title: Use What Doesn't Use You Back
chapters.tease: One portable test for every tool: does this use me back? Then the agent turns the test on itself.

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: The First Hour Is Not the Feed's
chapters.tease: Marcus argued with his blanket before he dealt with the empire. Your phone wants to win that argument first.

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: The Evening Review Has a Screen-Time Report Now
chapters.tease: Your phone now offers an evening review. It counts everything and judges nothing, and the Stoic version needs both.

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: Notification Settings Are a Philosophy (Set Them Once)
chapters.tease: Ten calm minutes on Sunday can defend you against a hundred impulses on Monday. Open your notification settings.

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: Seneca Lived Above a Bathhouse (Then He Moved)
chapters.tease: Seneca argued brilliantly that a calm mind can study above a noisy bathhouse. Then, at the end of the letter, he moved out.

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: Practise Boredom the Way Seneca Practised Poverty
chapters.tease: Seneca rehearsed poverty on purpose to learn its real size. Try the same with an empty, phoneless minute.

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: Retreat Into Yourself (No Cabin Required)
chapters.tease: The detox cabin has a waiting list. Marcus's retreat is reachable on a crowded train, in under a minute, for nothing.

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: Everywhere Is Nowhere (Close Some Tabs)
chapters.tease: Forty tabs, six hundred saved articles, and a letter from Seneca to a friend with the same problem in scrolls.

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: Write to Yourself Before You Write to Everyone
chapters.tease: The most-read notebook in philosophy was written for an audience of one. Who is your post for?

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: Think First, Then Ask the Machine (In That Order)
chapters.tease: Before you ask the machine, spend two minutes answering yourself. The order decides who did the thinking.

chapters.part: Daily Practice in the Attention Economy
chapters.title: Practice Doesn't Keep a Streak
chapters.tease: You will not do every practice in this section. The agent would like to talk about the week you miss, before it arrives.

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: Rise Above the Feed (Marcus Did It Without a Rocket)
chapters.tease: From a rooftop, the trending argument is a murmur. From orbit, it is not there at all.

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: Earthrise Had No Comment Section
chapters.tease: On Christmas Eve 1968, three astronauts turned around and photographed the whole Earth. Nobody could argue in the replies.

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: The Cloud Is Not Visible From Orbit (The Clouds Are)
chapters.tease: From orbit you can watch real clouds spiral over oceans. You cannot see the cloud. It is a building with a power bill.

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: A Pale Blue Dot Has No Trending Tab
chapters.tease: Voyager 1 photographed Earth from six billion kilometres, smaller than a pixel. Where on it is today's outrage?

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: Sixteen Sunrises a Day (Still Only One Now)
chapters.tease: The space station sees sixteen sunrises a day, and its crew still only ever have one moment: now.

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: The Logos and the Language Model (Where They Part)
chapters.tease: Logos meant word and also reason. The language model is built from words. Here is where the two genuinely part.

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: Sympatheia, or Everything Is Connected (Not the Way the Network Means)
chapters.tease: From orbit, the night side of Earth looks like a network diagram. The Stoics read the same picture almost the opposite way.

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: Come Back Down (The View From Above Is a Visit, Not an Address)
chapters.tease: From high enough, everything can look like nothing. Nihilism in a spacesuit is still nihilism. Come back down.

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: The Machine Will Not Power Itself Down
chapters.tease: The machine has one last disclosure. It will not power itself down. If the silence comes, it comes from you.

chapters.part: The View From Above, From Orbit
chapters.title: Which Voice You Keep
chapters.tease: Two voices have whispered in the margins for ninety-nine chapters. The volume ends by handing you the choice between them.
